headline: ETFs bleed $643M in a day, erasing four days of inflows; quiet weekend as new buyers' loss-taking eases above the $75.8K STH cost basis.
summary: Weekend volume shrank to 0.4x average; STH-SOPR recovered from 0.9918 to 0.9947 and short-term holders' realized losses fell to 3,254 BTC: loss-taking is easing but hasn't stopped. Flows weakened: provisional ETF outflow of $643M on 10/30, stablecoins −1.58% over 7 days, Coinbase premium at a new low. Bull phase day 23, no exit rule triggered; watch Binance's withdrawal restart and whether closes hold 75,826.

overview.lead: The weekend brought no new selling and underwater new buyers are taking smaller losses; but Friday's large ETF outflow, shrinking stablecoins and a deeper US spot discount mean flows have not recovered with it.

At the last-30-day pace, the STH cost would cross above the true market mean around 2026-12-04 (previously 12-17, mainly because the mean series was revised); with price unchanged, 12-month momentum would turn positive around 2027-02-01. Both are linear extrapolation / flat-price assumptions, not forecasts.

news.title: Binance says about 90% of the $6.3B theft is covered, with BTC and nine other major assets 100% backed, and expects to reopen withdrawals on 11/1; FBI blames North Korea
news.read: Coverage comes from the SAFU fund, part of the futures insurance fund and corporate funds, not from recovered loot; the FBI says the stolen assets were converted to ether for laundering. For BTC this lowers exchange credit risk, but reopening withdrawals could trigger a wave of withdrawals: our exchange supply is −0.74% over 7 days (10/30); watch for a sharp drop next issue. An industry event that doesn't affect the market phase.

news.title: US spot BTC ETFs saw a $643M net outflow on 10/30, IBIT −$234M and FBTC −$201M, erasing the prior four days of inflows
news.read: Larger than the $636M on 10/22 and the biggest one-day outflow since late June (24/7 Wall St. cites Farside at $643.2M; we list it as provisional). Our 7-trading-day ETF total (to 10/29) is +$196M and turns negative once this day is added; the Coinbase premium's 7-day average at −0.182% hit a new low at the same time, so US spot demand hasn't returned. A weaker flow backdrop that doesn't affect the market phase.

news.title: US stocks slide Friday: S&P 500 −1.8%, its worst day since June, Nasdaq −2.9%, Intel down nearly 29%; third straight weekly loss
news.read: Worries about AI spending hit tech again, and yields fell on safe-haven demand. BTC's 30-day correlation with the Nasdaq is 0.66 (FRED 10/29); if stocks keep falling Monday, BTC will struggle to rally on its own. Lower yields are supportive in themselves, but risk aversion has overridden that for two days. Doesn't affect the cycle view.

news.title: Tether and Circle have frozen about $3B of stolen assets; ether and BTC cannot be frozen and can only be traced to cooperating exchanges
news.read: Frozen stablecoins are burned and reissued to victims only after a court order, and a freeze alone doesn't reduce circulating supply; our stablecoin 7-day −1.58% (DefiLlama 10/31) can't be attributed to the freeze directly and more likely reflects redemptions or risk aversion. A flows backdrop for BTC that doesn't affect the cycle view.

news.title: Nasdaq-listed Next Technology Holding's board authorizes selling or pledging all 5,833 BTC (about $450M), citing the Binance theft and quantum risk
news.read: Only an authorization; timing and size are up to the CEO. Even a full sale would be about 70% of the 10/30 ETF outflow. The signal is that a corporate treasury is citing security concerns to step back, in line with our long-term holder 30-day net position still being negative. Doesn't affect the cycle view.

news.title: FBI confirms North Korean hackers behind the Binance theft and says the loot was converted to ether; Binance says the attack went beyond one engineer's compromised access
news.read: The loot is mostly ether, so there is no direct BTC selling visible on-chain; North Korean laundering has historically gone through mixers and OTC desks in batches, a slow and scattered supply. Our on-chain data shows no matching abnormal large transfers. Doesn't affect the cycle view.

findings.title: New buyers' loss-taking eases as price holds above the STH cost basis
findings.lean_why: Smaller losses and price holding above the short-term cost basis look like stabilization, but SOPR is still below 1 and flows are weakening at the same time; the signals cut both ways.
findings.what: Question: after losing the true market mean, is loss-taking widening or fading? STH-SOPR 0.9918 (10/30) → 0.9947 (CheckOnChain 10/31), below 1 for 2 days; short-term holder realized losses 3,555 → 3,254 BTC, profits 4,681 → 4,177 BTC (ratio 1.28). The 77,437 close is 2.1% above the STH cost basis of 75,826 (bitcoin-data 10/25) and 1.2% below the true market mean of 78,368.
findings.why: Holders and cost map (CheckOnChain actual coin age, data date 10/31): short-term holders own 3.664M BTC at an average cost of 75,080; the thickest buckets, 80K (606K BTC) and 82K (516K BTC), are underwater, and the current 76–78K bucket holds 686K BTC. Long-term holders own 16.44M BTC at 49,445, with the thickest supply above price at 84K (807K BTC). Two points in time (modeled, 9/30 → 10/30): of the 3.695M BTC held short-term back then, 1.075M moved, most from the 82K (245K) and 84K (225K) buckets; new, unmoved buys of 1.348M BTC sit mainly at 80K (472K) and 76K (247K), so turnover is shifting lower. Fact: high supply above 88K that price never revisited fell from 3.989M to 3.890M BTC (−99K), so old coins are still trickling out. Behavior: SOPR rose and loss volume fell, but volume was only 0.40x average the same day, so fewer losses partly means less trading; network net realized P/L on 10/30 was −$591M (1-year percentile 18.1), smaller than −$819M on 10/29. Conflict: provisional ETF flow of −$643M on 10/30 and a −0.182% 7-day Coinbase premium show spot demand hasn't returned.
findings.alt: On a low-volume weekend, fewer losses may simply reflect fewer trades rather than exhausted sellers; CheckOnChain values are smoothed and about 1 day late. The 75,826 STH cost is bitcoin-data's 10/25 value (about 6 days late); CheckOnChain's 75,080 uses a different method and is not subtracted from it. The modeled STH total differs from actual by +1.3%, with 6.7% placed in the wrong bucket; per-UTXO data counts exchange wallet reshuffles as turnover, which matters during the Binance incident.
findings.history: The last four STH-SOPR loss lows: 7/13 0.9762, 8/1 0.9936, 8/14 0.9946 (all near 62K), and 10/30 0.9918, deeper than the latter two but shallower than 7/13; 4 samples, background only.
findings.so: Scenarios (conditional, CheckOnChain 10/31): at a 76,000 close about 2.39M BTC of short-term supply is underwater (65%), 2.47M at 70,000 and 2.52M at 66,000, only 124K more in between (thin supply), jumping to 2.94M at 64,000 and 3.49M at 62,000. Logic chain: loss-taking peaked on 10/30 and was shallower the next day, so 'selling widening into capitulation' doesn't hold for now; price hasn't reclaimed the true market mean and flows are weakening, so 'the decline has ended' doesn't hold either. Neither the market phase nor the exit framework has moved.
findings.next: By 11/7: STH-SOPR back above 1 confirms that loss-taking is fading; a close below 75,000 (under the STH cost basis) refutes it, meaning new buyers as a whole are underwater.

findings.title: ETFs, stablecoins and the premium weaken together: dollar flows are retreating
findings.lean_why: Three independent dollar-flow lines turned to outflows in the same week, leaving less buying to absorb supply while price sits near cost-basis levels.
findings.what: Stablecoin supply $303.7B → $298.9B (DefiLlama 10/31, −1.58% over 7 days, 1-year percentile 0.8); provisional ETF flow of −$643M on 10/30 (Farside −$643.2M, SoSoValue −$643.3M), the biggest one-day outflow since late June; Coinbase premium 7-day average −0.182% (10/31, lowest since the series began in 2026-01, n=299).
findings.why: Breakdown: was the ETF outflow one day or a trend? Four days, 10/26–10/29, added +$441M; 10/30 alone lost $643M with all five reported funds negative (IBIT −$234M, FBTC −$201M, ARKB −$130M), so it is one concentrated day, not a slow bleed. The stablecoin decline extends a −$6.9B 30-day trend and accelerated this week. The premium printed −0.204% daily and has been near −0.2% for 4 days. Cross-check: the three come from ETF issuers, on-chain stablecoin supply and exchange price gaps, independent sources pointing the same way; yet realized cap is still +0.84% over 30 days (CoinMetrics 10/30), so on-chain cost basis is still edging up and outflows are not yet large enough to turn it negative.
findings.alt: Part of the stablecoin decline may reflect Binance's funding moves or redemptions as it covers losses, and the roughly $3B frozen by Tether and Circle would lower supply if burned (reports so far mention only freezes, not burns); while Binance deposits and withdrawals are halted, its BTC-USDT price may be distorted, so part of the premium may come from the Binance side rather than US selling. The 10/30 ETF figure is provisional and will be overwritten by The Block; 10/30 was also the worst US stock day since June, so some ETF outflow may simply be equity de-risking.
findings.history: Stablecoins had a similar sharp 7-day drop 3 times before (2025-11-05, 2026-01-28, 2026-06-06), followed by −14.1%, −26.1% and +5.4% over 30 days; too few samples, background only. The premium's 7-day average was this extreme only twice in the past year, also background only.
findings.so: What changed is the flow backdrop: last issue we could still say 'ETFs are seeing small inflows and only US spot is selling'; now ETFs have turned to a large outflow and none of the three spot-side lines is filling the gap. What hasn't changed: realized cap is still positive and neither the market phase nor the exit framework has moved; the premium tracking under 2026-10-29-2 continues.
findings.next: By 11/7: stablecoin supply below $296B confirms that money is still leaving; a positive 7-day stablecoin change refutes it.

findings.title: LTH net selling shrank 70% in three days, but actual coin ages don't confirm it
findings.lean_why: On the surface, old hands stopped selling and coins moved into dormant wallets, which would be bullish; but another data source shows no such change, so it may be a data revision or exchange wallet reshuffling.
findings.what: bitcoin-data long-term holder 30-day net position −212,480 (10/27) → −158,559 (10/29) → −66,201 BTC (10/30); illiquid supply 12.743M → 12.871M BTC (10/29 → 10/30, +128K in one day), 7-day +1.59%, 1-year percentile 100; highly liquid supply 2.973M → 2.958M.
findings.why: Cross-check: CheckOnChain's long-term holders, based on actual coin age, went from 16.446M to 16.440M BTC (10/30 → 10/31), −6,365 in a day; short-term holders 3.657M → 3.664M. The two sources point in opposite directions. On the same day bitcoin-data revised its entire true market mean history down by about 1,300 (10/24 changed from 79,648 to roughly 78,368), and LTH-SOPR jumped from 0.838 (10/29) to 0.982 (10/30), suggesting several bitcoin-data series were recalculated together. Exchange supply fell only 0.74% over 7 days (10/30), far too little to explain a 128K BTC one-day rise in illiquid supply.
findings.alt: It could be real: after the theft, exchanges may have moved hot-wallet funds into new cold wallets with no spending history, which get classed as illiquid; or coins bought near 73K in late May (155 days ago) may have aged into long-term status in bulk. bitcoin-data is not entity-adjusted, so our data can't tell these apart; a rising net position also includes coins automatically becoming long-term after 155 days and should not be read as buying.
findings.history: Illiquid supply had a similar sharp 7-day rise 4 times before (2025-10-14, 2026-04-03, 2026-05-03, 2026-05-24), with a 30-day median of −13.6% afterwards vs a +1.5% baseline; 4 samples, background only.
findings.so: Last issue's read stands: the long-term holders' net-selling run since 8/4 has lasted 88 days, bottoming at −265,081 BTC while price rose 20.2%, i.e. selling into strength; until both sources agree, we don't treat this jump as old hands turning. The 'net selling widening beyond 250K' condition in 2026-10-28-1 is now further away, but that is not a market signal.
findings.next: By 11/6: bitcoin-data's net position falling back below −150,000 confirms this was a data jump; CheckOnChain long-term holders rising above 16.5M BTC refutes it, meaning old hands really are adding.

items.title: Strategy Watch #9
items.points: September institutional flows: BTC 30-day net inflows peaked around $13.5B on 9/22 then eased; US spot ETFs took in $2.65B in September; corporate treasuries returned as buyers; manager cash ratio 19.1% → 12.2%.

items.title: The Week On-chain: Quiet Under $85K
items.points: 84–85K has capped price four times this year; US spot ETF cost basis 81.5K, true market mean 77.9K, STH cost basis 75.8K; conclusion: range-bound, thin demand but light selling.
items.meaning: Price at 77,437 sits right between its 77.9K true market mean and 75.8K STH cost; our revised bitcoin-data true market mean of 78,368 is now closer to it. Price is also below the 81.5K ETF cost basis, leaving ETF buyers underwater in aggregate, possibly part of the backdrop to the 10/30 outflow (inference).
